subject: Literature

questions.text: This paper consists of sections A, B and C with a total of ten (10) questions.
Cellular phones and any unauthorized materials are not allowed in the examination room.
Write your Examination Number on every page of your answer booklet(s).
For each of the items (i) - (x), choose the correct answer from among the given alternatives and write its letter beside the item number in the answer booklet provided.

Which of the following feature distinguishes oral literature from other forms of literature? Stored in books and tape recorder Uses gestures to add flavour Expensive to produce Delivered by writing Property of an individual person Choose Answer : - -
In what type of drama does the main character end up in death or danger? Drama Melodrama Tragic drama Monodrama Comedy drama Choose Answer : - -
As you compose a poem, you create an atmosphere of feelings and emotions. What is the name of this poetic device? Irony Sarcasm Mood Diction Poetic licence Choose Answer : - -
Which of the following terms is used to refer to the tools used for appreciating literary works? Language devices Sense devices Poetic devices Artistic devices Artistic style Choose Answer : - -
What does this poetic line stand for? “Ten bucks you say I owe you?” Litotes Irony Sarcasm Rhetoric Paradox Choose Answer : - -
Which of the following is a guideline for the directors and actors during dramatising? Drama Novel Novella Play Novelette Choose Answer : - -
If a person wrote a book and put some brief explanations on the back cover about the book and himself/herself, this book is called Parable Tale Song Critic novel Choose Answer : - -
Which figure of speech is useful when you want to reduce the impact of harsh words in writing a work of art? Personification Euphemism Diction Hyperbole Suspense Choose Answer : - -
Which of these best distinguish literature from other subjects like Chemistry? Plot and topics No numbers and signs Topic and similes Content and plot Plot and figures of speech Choose Answer : - -
A word which is offensive and forbidden to be used is known as irony hyperbole taboo barbarism litotes Choose Answer : - -

Match the descriptions in List A with the corresponding type of figure of speech in List B by writing the letter of the correct response beside the item number in the answer booklet(s) provided. List A List B Animals may speak, objects may dance or even feel “it stinks, it is rotten” Time is money “Ooh! What a person you are, you killed a mosquito!” He knows a lot of things; he is a man of books. Metaphor Sarcasm Hyperbole Metonymy Imagery Personification Paradox View Ans

Differentiate the following literary terms: (a) Narrative poem and Lyric poem View Ans (b) Metaphor and Simile View Ans (c) Irony and Satire View Ans (d) Poetic devices and Poetic licence View Ans (e) Flashback and Foreshadowing View Ans

Read the following poem and then answer the questions that follow: Time of Martyrdom – David Diop The white killed my father My father was proud The white raped my mother My mother was beautiful The white bent my brother under the sun of the roads My brother was strong The white turned toward me His hands red with black blood And said in his Master’s voice “Boy” an easy chair, a towel, water! Questions (a) What is the poem about? View Ans (b) What type of poem is this? Give a reason to your answer. View Ans (c) Briefly explain two themes found in the poem. View Ans (d) Briefly explain two poetic devices used in the poem. View Ans (e) Briefly explain the relevance of the poem to the society. View Ans

In each of the expression (a) - (e) state the function which each one performs in literature. (a) When literature makes people to enjoy their society. View Ans (b) Literature can make people to respond positively about what is happening in the society. View Ans (c) The time when evils happen in the society literature does not keep quite. View Ans (d) When people are ignorant about something happening in their society such as a terrible disease like CORONA, then through literature they get to know it. View Ans (e) When there are dangerous things in the society and literature always stop people from doing those things. View Ans

Write the word that describes each of the description in items (a) - (e) . (a) The written script of drama. View Ans (b) Conversation of characters. View Ans (c) The writer’s descriptions of sets, characters and actions. View Ans (d) The written script is normally divided into one or more major divisions. View Ans (e) Subdivisions that are concerned with single event and may happen in a single setting. View Ans
Choose two main characters from two novels and show how they reflect our everyday life situation. Write three points from each novel. View Ans
‘Children as the future generation of a society encounter difficulties.’ Show how true this statement is by referring to two poems read under this programme. Give three points for each poem. View Ans

Referring to three plays ‘The Trials of Brother Jero’ by Wole Soyinka, “Dilemma of a Ghost’ by Christina Ama Aidoo and ‘The Lion and the Jewel’ by Wole Soyinka, write the causes of conflicts in African societies. Give two points from each play. View Ans

With reference to the play ‘The Lion and the Jewel’ by Wole Soyinka and ‘The Trials of Brother Jero’ by Wole Soyinka, from each play analyse three themes that are found in each play and state reasons for choosing those themes. View Ans
